inspect: Jim's pantry. Padlocked. Jim has the key on a string round his neck and has never once taken it off, not even for the Grand Nap.
Beans. Red beans, white beans, black beans, baked beans. Family-size beans. Emergency beans. Travel beans, in a little tin with a handle.
One can of Spicy Stench Sauce where the salt should be. No salt.
A vat of Spicy Stench Sauce, bought in bulk. The lid is bulging. Every so often it ticks, like it's thinking.
A vat of Spicy Stench Sauce, vented. CONTENTS MAY PRESSURIZE AFTER OPENING. They did. The lid is in a beam above you. Most of the sauce is on the walls.
The blender. A jar, a crank, a vacuum tube that lights up for no reason, and a fork, wired in where the blades should be.
There is still smoothie in it. It is still moving.
A kerosene lamp, turned up much too high, next to a television made of a turnip crate, over a floor of bean sacks, under a hammock full of Grand Stenchmaster.
The one luxury pillow. Satin, piped, gold tassels. The only thing anybody has ever got back out of the Great Sharkstorm.
It is communal. There's a rota. Garrick is not on the rota.
The sharks' leftovers: lobster shells, crab shells, a foil tray of oyster shells, an empty caviar tin, a takeout box, napkins, a little fork. Dumped on your deck from a height.
